title: New Capital Civic Headquarters
caption: Fig. — Precast fin façade; plant is hidden in the crown and a single basement spine.
headline: A six-storey civic building with no visible plant and 31% less cooling energy than the code baseline.
brief: The architect's precast-fin façade left no room for louvres, and the client wanted a roofscape without visible plant. We had to fit a full district-cooling interface, standby generation and a 46,000 m² air-conditioning system into a building whose elevations could not show a single grille.
approach: Moved all air-handling plant into a continuous crown level behind the fins, using the fin depth itself as the intake plenum.
Selected dedicated outdoor-air units with enthalpy wheels and chilled beams for the office floors, halving duct sizes and recovering ceiling height.
Ran an hourly energy model (EnergyPlus) at every stage so façade and plant decisions were tested against one baseline.
Issued a federated LOD 350 model to the contractor with zero hard clashes at tender.

outcomes.label: less cooling energy than the ASHRAE 90.1 baseline
hard clashes in the tender model
ceiling height recovered on office floors

title: Al Rawda Specialist Hospital
caption: Fig. — Main atrium; smoke control and daylight were designed together.
headline: A 180-bed hospital where twelve operating theatres share one resilient, fully redundant plant.
brief: The operator needed a phased hospital that could open its outpatient wing a year before the theatres, without temporary plant, and meet FGI pressure-cascade requirements from day one.
approach: Split the central plant into N+1 modules sized so the outpatient phase ran on two of five chillers at a good part-load efficiency.
Designed theatre and isolation-room airflow with laminar-flow canopies and monitored pressure cascades on the BMS.
Engineered medical gas, nurse call and IT networks as one coordinated ELV package to simplify procurement.
Wrote a staged commissioning plan so each wing could be handed over without disturbing live clinical areas.

outcomes.label: redundancy on chillers, AHUs and generators
early opening of the outpatient wing

title: Sokhna Logistics Data Hall
caption: Fig. — Coordinated services zone above the white space, LOD 350.
headline: A 1.2 MW edge data hall designed for a coastal climate, with free cooling for a third of the year.
brief: A port operator needed resilient on-site compute for terminal automation. Salt-laden air, high humidity and limited utility capacity ruled out a copy-paste data-centre design.
approach: Compared four cooling topologies on lifetime cost; selected indirect evaporative units with DX trim to keep salt air out of the white space.
Designed a 2N electrical path with lithium-ion UPS, sized against the utility's actual available capacity.
Specified inert-gas suppression and VESDA early-warning detection zoned to the containment aisles.
Coordinated cable trays, busways and ductwork in a single model with the structural steel.

title: Zamalek Office Retrofit & Energy Audit
caption: Fig. — Thermal survey overlaid on the existing services drawings.
headline: A 1970s office building brought to modern comfort standards while occupied, with a 3.4-year payback.
brief: Split units on every balcony, tripping breakers in summer and an electricity bill that kept rising. The owner wanted a retrofit that tenants would barely notice.
approach: Measured before designing: a two-week logging campaign and thermal imaging of every floor.
Replaced 140 split units with a VRF system routed through the existing light wells.
Added LED lighting with daylight dimming and sub-metering per tenant.
Phased the works floor by floor over weekends.

title: Sahl Hasheesh Beach Resort
headline: A 410-key resort where every drop of water is treated, reused or desalinated on site.
brief: No reliable municipal water and a remote site: the resort had to produce, treat and reuse its own water while keeping guest-facing areas silent and invisible.
approach: Designed a reverse-osmosis plant with energy recovery and a sewage treatment plant feeding irrigation.
Used heat recovery from chillers for domestic hot water across all guest blocks.
Laid out the services corridors so plant noise never reached guest rooms (NR 25).

outcomes.label: of hot water from recovered heat

title: Nile University Research Labs
headline: Wet and dry laboratories with demand-controlled ventilation, designed to LEED Gold.
brief: Labs are the most energy-hungry buildings on a campus. The university wanted safe, flexible lab space without a lab-sized energy bill.
approach: Applied demand-controlled ventilation tied to air-quality sensing in each lab.
Specified high-plume exhaust fans and run-around heat recovery.
Designed modular service spines so labs can be reconfigured without new risers.

outcomes.label: air changes per hour when unoccupied
lower HVAC energy than a constant-volume design
